ezekiel.47.p1.b1.text: Then the man brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing from under the threshold of the temple toward the east …

ezekiel.47.p1.b2.text: As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through ankle-deep water.

ezekiel.47.p1.b3.text: Then he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through knee-deep water. Again he measured a thousand cubits and led me through waist-deep water.

ezekiel.47.p1.b4.text: Once again he measured off a thousand cubits, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough for swimming—a river that could not be crossed on foot.

ezekiel.47.p2.b1.text: Son of man, do you see this?

ezekiel.47.p2.b2.text: This water flows out to the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah. When it empties into the Sea … wherever the river flows, everything will flourish.

ezekiel.47.p2.b3.text: Fishermen will stand by the shore; from En-gedi to En-eglaim they will spread their nets

ezekiel.47.p3.b1.text: Each month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing.

ezekiel.47.p3.b2.text: These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel … this land will fall to you as an inheritance.

ezekiel.47.p3.b3.text: You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you, they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
